name: Modelize
summary: Shopify app that generates on-model, lifestyle, studio and flat-lay product photos in bulk from your existing catalogue images, using Google's Gemini image models.
best_for: Shopify fashion, jewellery and homeware sellers who need consistent on-model, lifestyle or flat-lay imagery across a large catalogue and cannot justify a photographer per drop
skip_if: you need art direction a preset cannot express, photography of the actual physical item in its real texture, or a vendor with a long public track record: this app launched in April 2026
honest_knock: The economics are flat: at roughly $0.19 to $0.20 an image on every tier, moving up the ladder buys resolution, custom presets and support, never a cheaper image. Read it that way and the pricing is honest; read it as a volume discount and you will overbuy. Two other things deserve a clear head. The output quality rides on Google's Gemini image models rather than on anything Modelize owns, so results and consistency can shift when Google ships a new version, and that is outside the vendor's control as much as yours. And the app is new (launched 20 April 2026, 26 reviews on 4 October 2026) so the rating is a small sample, not a track record. Finally, an on-model photo generated by AI shows a person who does not exist; check what your ad platforms and marketplaces require you to disclose before you build a catalogue on it.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Starter · per month for 100 AI images
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-09-17, 2026-10-04 and 2026-11-12 on apps.shopify.com/modelize; listed in October as “Modelize: AI Product Photos” and on 12 November as “Modelize: AI Image Generator”) Free plan available, then Starter $19, Pro $49 and Enterprise $99 a month — the three paid rates are unchanged since 19 August 2026. The free tier was raised from 3 to 10 AI images, still one-time rather than per month, with built-in presets and models at standard 2K. Starter covers 100 images a month with 3 AI custom presets and 3 custom models, standard 2K and email support. Pro at $49 covers 250 images, 10 custom presets and 10 custom models, resolution up to 4K and priority support. Enterprise at $99 includes 500 images with $0.20 per additional image, unlimited custom presets and models, maximum 4K and dedicated support. The annual option is gone: on modelize.studio/pricing, read the same day and again on 4 October 2026, all three paid tiers are labelled “Billed month to month” and the page carries no yearly rate and no two-months-free wording anywhere, where in August it sold Free, Starter and Pro annually. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 4.9 from 26 App Store reviews on 4 October 2026 (25 at five stars, one at three), against 25 reviews on 17 September and 5.0 from 13 reviews on 19 August. Developer Optify, 16 Rue Cuvier, Lyon, France; the app launched 20 April 2026 and carries Shopify’s “Built for Shopify” badge. On 12 November 2026 the listing and modelize.studio/pricing showed the same four tiers, allowances and amounts, every paid tier still “Billed month to month”, and the rating stood at 4.8 from 28 reviews (26 at five stars, one at four, one at three). The listing now names Gemini Nano Banana 2 and Nano Banana Pro as the image models.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 16 November 2026 the session tested Modelize on the Free plan of a Shopify development store: one AI model photo of a snowboard, its automatic publication on the product, the credit use, the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen and the uninstall dialog. Nothing was paid, approved or uninstalled. Create: Add products, the product The Complete Snowboard ticked and added, Images per product set to 1 (the default was 3), Choose styles, Browse styles, a search for model, the style On Model - Outdoor, Done and Generate 1 image; about 12 clicks. The source was the existing product photo of the snowboard; no person or face was uploaded. The cost was shown before the run: 1 image, 1 credit and 9 credits left after this run; with Auto and 3 images it read 3 images, 3 credits and 7 credits left. The run took about 1 minute (Generating 0 of 1. You can leave this page, the run keeps going.) and ended Completed with the image On Model - Outdoor marked Published. The output shows an AI generated woman in a winter coat holding the turquoise snowboard in front of a snowy mountain; by eye the board has a similar colour and pattern to the original, which is a tester impression and not measured. The image was published on the product in Shopify automatically, without a separate confirmation. The buttons are Replace on product, Remove from Shopify, Download and Open full size; editing with AI offers Background, Model, Pose and Custom at 0.5 credits per edit with 9 left. Afterwards the plan page said 9 of 10 credits left. The product search field in the picker did not filter, the list stayed complete, and scrolling by hand worked. The storefront preview was not viewed and the theme was not touched. Timing, approximate tester observations: Create at about 14:17, the run at 2:17 PM and the image published at 2:18 PM, so about 2 minutes from install to the first image, of which about 1 minute was the generation. Uninstall: Settings, Apps, the menu for Modelize offers Open app, View data and Uninstall; the Uninstall Modelize dialog (reason list, feedback box, Uninstall disabled until a reason is chosen) was opened and cancelled. There was no paid subscription to cancel. Not tested: bulk generation, Auto mode, video, own styles and models, 4K, Pro and Enterprise, a fashion or jewellery product (only a snowboard), the resolution of the image, the theme view of the published image, a real payment and cancelling a paid plan, and the chat widget. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The generated image was published on the product automatically, without a confirmation step, and the app showed a 404 right after installing until the page was reloaded.

sessions.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. We ran Modelize on 16 November 2026 on the Free plan of a Shopify development store. We picked one snowboard and the style On Model - Outdoor, set Images per product to 1, and generated. The screen showed the cost first: 1 image, 1 credit, 9 credits left after the run. The run took about 1 minute and the finished image was published on the product in Shopify without a separate confirmation. The plan page then read 9 of 10 credits left. From install to the first image took about 2 minutes. We read the plan screens up to the Shopify approval screen for Starter and opened the uninstall dialog; we paid, approved and uninstalled nothing. The full run, with clicks, timings and what we did not test, is in the exit test section below.
findings: Credits: the screen quoted 1 credit for 1 image before the run, and the counter after it fell from 10 to 9. Auto mode with 3 images quoted 3 credits.
Publishing: the image went onto the product in Shopify the moment the run finished. We were not asked to confirm, and Remove from Shopify sat one click away in the library.
Free plan: the plan card lists one custom preset and one custom model a month, where our earlier notes said none. We did not try either.
Starter: $19 for 30 days on the card and on the Shopify approval screen, with no trial line. We did not see a tax line and approved nothing.
not_tested: Output at scale: bulk runs, Auto mode and video were not run; one snowboard is the whole sample, and we measured no image size.
Money: no payment was made and no paid plan was cancelled, so Starter, Pro and Enterprise are read from screens only.
Fit for other products: a fashion or jewellery item, our own styles and models, and the published image in the live theme.
Everything else: support, the chat widget, invitations, export and reimport. We created the store and verified his identity himself.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
